independence_declaration.statement: I am domain-reviewer, run T-DG1-REV-DOM-R10. I authored no implementation, register text or decision in the DG1 scope. The round-10 repairs are the F-DG1-130 setEngine ban and member audit in architecture.testkit.ts/architecture.test.ts (T-DG1-BE11, backend-workflow-engineer) and the F-DG1-131 rewording of D-055 (delivery-orchestrator). I did not raise either finding (code-security-reviewer did), and I did not author either fix. I formed this verdict before reading any other reviewer's round-10 record, and none was visible to me (docs/delivery/reviews/DG1/round-10 did not exist when I started). The earlier review material I used: my own role's round-9 record and harness scripts (re-used as round-10 copies with only headers, diff ranges and the findings list changed), the findings.json entries for F-DG1-130/131, the T-DG1-BE11 handback, and D-055. I grant no business, Finance or IT approval. Product gate G6 is not engineering gate DG7.

Compare its usage statement with an independent TypeScript-AST inventory of node: specifiers, `process` identifiers and process.<member> in src/modules/**. checks_run.actual: F-DG1-131 is fixed. The false sentence ('the only node built-ins module source imports are the seven listed and the only process members are the four listed') is gone. D-055 now says module source imports four of the seven (crypto, fs, path, url) and uses none of the four process members, and calls the rest 'reviewed safe headroom … NOT claimed as current usage'. My independent AST inventory gives exactly [crypto, fs, path, url] (crypto x5, path x3, fs x1, url x1) and zero `process` identifiers or members, both asserted. D-055 also now describes the module-vs-member scope and the F-DG1-130 member audit. Residual accuracy gap, raised as proposed F-DG1-011 (Low, non-mandatory): D-055 calls the member audit 'exhaustive', re-run 'when the Node floor/target changes', without naming the runtime it ran on. The testkit header says 'Node v22.22.2' and the handback says 'Node 24, the production target, is BLOCKED', so the target has never been audited. D-055 also keeps 'closes the whole loader/exec class at once … prevents further adjacent-route findings', which F-DG1-130 disproved and which a later sentence in the same row contradicts. Its Evidence column still cites the round-9 counts 101/101 and 294/294 (now 105/105 and 298/298). The testkit header and the handback are accurate. This is decision-record wording only, with no capability impact.

checks_run.procedure: Run an independent probe written by me to show the F-DG1-130 fix does not over-reach. (1) moduleViolations is zero for every module. (2) An AST inventory written separately from the testkit scanner. (3) Eleven positive controls must each give [] (asserted): node:crypto randomUUID/createHash, createHmac/randomBytes/timingSafeEqual, namespace randomUUID + webcrypto.getRandomValues, default-import getHashes, fs/promises, url+path, util+os, process.env/argv/once/exit, decimal.js, and identifiers merely containing 'Engine' (setEngineLabel, engineName). (4) Ten setEngine forms must each be denied: named, aliased, namespace, string key, destructured, renamed destructure, constructed key, template key, re-export, dynamic import. (5) Eighteen loader/debug/exec/network controls must still be denied (no regression).
checks_run.command: cp 03-default-deny-overreach-probe.test.ts apps/api/src/zz-dom-r10-probe.test.ts (clone only); npx vitest run --project unit-node apps/api/src/zz-dom-r10-probe.test.ts --reporter=verbose
checks_run.environment: disposable clone at 265af7e; the probe file was never in the candidate tree and was removed from the clone after the run
checks_run.expected: 5/5 pass; positive controls []; every setEngine form and every negative control at least 1 violation
checks_run.actual: 5 passed (5), exit 0. All 11 positive controls give [], so importing node:crypto and using randomUUID/createHash/createHmac/randomBytes/timingSafeEqual/webcrypto/getHashes stays allowed. Identifiers that merely contain 'Engine' are not flagged. All 10 setEngine forms are denied ('native loader via setEngine', '.setEngine()', '["setEngine"]', 'a destructured setEngine'; the constructed key is caught by the non-literal computed-key rule). All 18 regression controls are denied. Observation, not a defect: the ban is name-based, like require/eval, so a module that declared its own function named exactly `setEngine` would be flagged. No module does, and the cost is a rename.

checks_run.procedure: As a sanity check of the testkit header's F-DG1-130 member audit (common note: a member the audit already cleared is not a new finding), scan by name every own property of node:{crypto, fs, fs/promises, os, path, url, util} plus fs.promises, path.posix/win32, util.types, crypto.webcrypto/subtle and *.constants on this Node. Use a loader-like regex (load|engine|dlopen|exec|spawn|fork|eval|require|import|module|debug|native|binding|wasm|compile|script|inspect|worker|fips|open|run|plugin|extension|process), and check the type of every hit the header does not explicitly clear.
checks_run.command: node docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/domain/round-10/05-member-name-scan.mjs; node -e '<typeof os.constants.dlopen / fs.openAsBlob / crypto.constants.ENGINE_METHOD_ALL / crypto.getFips>'
checks_run.environment: node v22.22.2, OpenSSL 3.5.5 (repository; read-only scan, nothing written except the evidence file)
checks_run.expected: no loader member other than crypto.setEngine (banned); every other hit cleared by the header or harmless
checks_run.actual: The hits are crypto.setEngine (banned), setFips/getFips, the ENGINE_METHOD_* numeric constants, fs open/opendir/truncate/openAsBlob (file I/O), os.loadavg, os.constants.dlopen, util.debug/debuglog/inspect/isNullOrUndefined and util.types.isModuleNamespaceObject/isNativeError. The header does not name os.constants.dlopen, crypto.getFips, fs.openAsBlob or the ENGINE_METHOD_* constants. os.constants.dlopen is a plain object of RTLD_* numbers ({RTLD_LAZY:1,…}), the flags for the banned process.dlopen. getFips is a read-only query. openAsBlob reads a file. The constants are numbers. None is a loader, so the audit's conclusion holds on Node 22.22.2. BLOCKED part: Node 24 (the production target) could not be scanned. This sandbox has only node20/21/22 and no network. That is why F-DG1-011 asks D-055 to state it.

summary: PASS with one new Low, non-mandatory finding. F-DG1-131 is verified closed. D-055 no longer claims the allow-lists equal real usage. It now says 4 of 7 built-ins are used (crypto/fs/path/url), none of the 4 process members, and the rest is reviewed safe headroom, and my independent AST inventory confirms this exactly. The F-DG1-130 fix does not over-reach. The real module tree is clean, and node:crypto with randomUUID/createHash/createHmac/randomBytes/timingSafeEqual/webcrypto stays allowed. All 10 setEngine forms I wrote are denied, and a member-name scan on Node 22.22.2 finds no other loader member. There is no regression: the only product-tree change is two build-excluded test files. On the frozen candidate sha256:18fee161…c8807: unit 298/298, architecture 105/105, probe 5/5, integration 200/200 twice with 0 57P01, live AR/EN 108/108 (closure 422/G6, scoped access, identity, cursor pagination, provisional branding, Unknown states). Static checks are clean, and the register is unchanged with complete evidence. The round-9 domain closures hold. New finding, proposed F-DG1-011 (Low, non-mandatory, documentation only): D-055 calls the member audit 'exhaustive' without naming its Node 22.22.2-only runtime. Node 24, the production target, is BLOCKED in the handback. D-055 also keeps the disproved 'prevents further adjacent-route findings' sentence. Node 24 could not be checked here (no binary, no network).
